newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open higher on stronger golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open higher on stronger golds.

text.p: * Toronto stocks opened higher as expected on Thursday, as stronger bullion prices boosted the shares of gold producers. * 6.69 million shares changed hands, worth C$88.29 million.
Toronto stocks opened higher as expected on Thursday as a rise in bullion helped strengthen shares of gold producers.
"Gold's up a couple of bucks so there are a lot of guys hoping it's bottomed out here. So you're just seeing some buying, bottom-fishing, whatever you want to call it," one Toronto-based trader said.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index opened higher, rising 9.30 points to 6583.91 on turnover of 6.69 million shares worth C$88.29 million. There were 226 advancing stocks, 168 decliners and 215 unchanged.
Eleven of the TSE's 14 subgroups rose in early trade. Shares of gold producers recorded the strongest gains, rising 119.88 points or 1.59 percent.
Comex gold rose US$1.80 on Thursday to US$320.70, after earlier this week touching 12-year lows.

Shares of oil producers weighed heavily on the market, falling 0.88 percent. Among the worst performing oil stocks was Renaissance Energy Ltd. The Calgary-based company tumbled 2.90 to 36.40 with more than 580,000 shares changing hands.
* Barrick Gold Corp, the world's second largest gold producer, helped lead the market higher, rising 0.70 to 29.65 with more than 130,000 shares changings hands.
* Alcan Aluminium Ltd rose 0.20 to 48.55 in thin trade. The world largest aluminum producer is expected to report second-quarter earnings later in the session.
